name: orchestration
summary: Type /build and say what you want: small work goes straight to a pull request, big work becomes a map that a conductor thread works through, and side work gets its own thread.
day: You type /build and say what you want. The agent sizes the work: a small change goes straight to a draft pull request, a feature gets one plan to approve, and a large change becomes a map, where a conductor thread starts one worker thread per ticket. A side fix starts in its own thread.
cost: Each worker thread spends your AI plan's usage like any thread. Maps live as issues in a repo you name.
risk: A conductor starts worker threads without asking for each one. Each pull request still stays a draft until you say otherwise.

settings.question: Which repo's issues hold your maps? Leave it empty to use your context repo, or your Hedge profile repo when you have none.
Which file holds the lessons log that maps read and write, such as a path in a private repo?
Which file logs your rollouts, one JSON line per stage, so hedge lessons can name holds and rollbacks? ~/ is allowed.
Where do your team's goals live, so a map can name the metric its work moves?
Which analytics project shows how people use your product?
Which mark starts a closing line that waits on someone else, so the thread snoozes?
Which mark starts a closing line that snoozes the thread until the time on the line?
Which mark starts a closing line that settles the thread until its own scheduled check?
Which mark starts a closing line that says the work is done and you may settle the thread?
For how many days does a closing line that waits on someone else snooze the thread?
In which time zone are the times on a snooze line, such as Europe/Berlin? Leave it empty to use this machine's time zone.

workflows.name: Planning maps
workflows.sentence: Big work becomes a map of tickets, and a conductor thread works through it with one worker thread per ticket.

workflows.name: Side threads
workflows.sentence: When you agree to a side fix, it starts in its own T3 thread, and this thread stays on its task.

workflows.name: Question guard
workflows.sentence: A top-level T3 thread that ends its turn with a decision for you in prose is stopped once and told to ask with the question tool, so the decision reaches you even while the thread waits on a watch. An agent message that would interrupt a thread waiting on your answer is turned back once and told to queue, so the question stays open. A T3 thread that owns an open pull request and ends its turn while the proof gate has not passed at the pushed head is sent back once, with the step still owed.

workflows.name: Closing-line parking
workflows.sentence: A top-level T3 thread parks itself by the mark its last line starts with. A wait on someone else snoozes it for a few days, a snooze line snoozes it until its time, and a line that names its own scheduled check settles it once the turn ends. A thread you pinned stays in view, and a thread that settles while it alone links an open pull request is sent back once.
